subject: Charter Commission Home Rule Petition
overview: The City Council considered a proposed Home Rule Petition to establish an elected Charter Commission and referred the measure to the Committee of the Whole. The Council also approved resolutions concerning state municipal aid, tax-exempt institution regulations, local food security goals, and opposition to expanded live entertainment at Encore Casino.

items.title: Public Hearing on Automotive Repair License for 38 Harvard Avenue
items.summary: The Council continued the public hearing for OBE's Auto Service to the next meeting to resolve questions regarding special permit procedures.

items.title: Resolution of Condolence for Frank Palmisano
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution extending condolences to the family of Frank Palmisano.

items.title: Home Rule Petition for Charter Commission
items.summary: The Council referred a proposed Home Rule Petition establishing an elected nine-member Charter Commission to the Committee of the Whole for further review.

items.title: Resolution Regarding DPW Salt Mix
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution requesting a report from the DPW commissioner on whether the city's road salt mix is pet-friendly.

items.title: Resolution Requesting Youth Commission Draft Ordinance
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution requesting that the city solicitor provide a draft ordinance establishing a Youth Commission.

items.title: Resolution on Snow Emergency Parking Procedures and Communications
items.summary: The Council approved an amended resolution requesting the administration explore temporary and permanent solutions to improve resident notifications during snow emergencies.

items.title: Resolution Opposing Encore Casino Entertainment Venue Expansion
items.summary: The Council approved sending a letter to the Massachusetts Gaming Commission opposing live entertainment venue proposals at Encore Casino that violate surrounding community agreements.

items.title: Resolution on Public Art Location Planning
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution requesting that city departments identify public art locations and establish interest forms while considering equity and gentrification impacts.

items.title: Zoning Amendment Proposal for Cannabis Labor Peace Agreements
items.summary: The Council tabled a proposed zoning amendment requiring labor peace agreements and construction labor plans for cannabis facilities pending legal opinions.

items.title: Resolutions Supporting State Legislation on Tax-Exempt Entities
items.summary: The Council approved resolutions endorsing state legislation regarding municipal PILOT frameworks, lost property tax studies, and institutional master plan requirements.

items.title: Resolution Supporting Increased Unrestricted General Government Aid
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution urging state leaders to increase unrestricted general government aid in the FY2023 state budget.

items.title: Resolution Reaffirming Pledge for a Hunger-Free Medford by 2028
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution reaffirming the city's commitment to end hunger by 2028 and supporting expanded local food security capacity.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: The Council briefly removed personnel ordinance amendments from the table before re-tabling them to clarify legal voting requirements.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council approved Committee of the Whole reports from February 1 and February 2, 2022.
